svg.title: AssignAgvs consumes a shallow copy of the DAG
svg.desc: Rounds of AssignAgvs: the copy loses its roots one by one while ctx->event_dag gains AGV events; both point at the same event objects.
svg.metadata: ["Start: the copy has the same six events (the same objects) as ctx->event_dag. Its roots, a and e, are the events with no unprocessed prerequisite.", "Phase 1 drains the non-tray roots: the bay transition a is applied to working_state and removed from the copy. Removing a makes b a root. ctx->event_dag is unchanged.", "Phase 2 matches AGVs to the TrayMove roots b and e (BottleneckAssignment), calls SetAgvId on them and removes them from the copy. Their approach, lift and lower events are added to ctx->event_dag only.", "Round 2: no non-tray roots, so phase 2 matches c and f. Their AGV events go into ctx->event_dag; d becomes the only root.", "Round 3: d is applied and removed. The copy is empty and the loop ends; OrderAgvMovesAfterBlockingAgvs, RemoveRedundantEdges() and OrderAllTransitionsAroundAgvLifts then run on ctx->event_dag."]

g.text: Every SetAgvId(...) on a root of the copy is visible in ctx->event_dag: both DAGs hold the same TrayMove objects. New AGV events are added only to ctx->event_dag, so they never become roots of the copy.
